> **What this case shows** — the ACF told us how long the signal's memory is, the PACF told us its
> order; the **autoregressive (AR) model** turns that into a *generative description*. This case adds
> the fit itself — **`arYuleWalker`**, solving the Yule-Walker equations from the ACF via
> Durbin-Levinson. On a real eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces
> **`statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method="mle")`** **bit-for-bit** — both the AR coefficients
> (max |diff| ~**5e-15**) and the innovation variance — and the fitted AR(4) is **stationary**, with a
> parametric spectrum that peaks in the **alpha band** (~12 Hz).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `arYuleWalker(x, order)` → AR coefficients + innovation variance.
**Way of thinking** — an AR model says "the next sample is a weighted sum of the last p, plus noise".
Its coefficients are the memory; its innovation variance is what's left unpredicted; and its spectrum
is a low-parameter alternative to the periodogram — sharp where the dynamics are resonant.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::arYuleWalker()`, with `partialAutocorrelation()` for the order.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `arYuleWalker` reproduces `statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method="mle")`
bit-for-bit for the AR(4) coefficients (max |diff| ~5e-15) and the innovation variance (~5e-13); the fit
is stationary (all roots outside the unit circle), and its spectrum peaks at ~12 Hz.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and its payoff: having added the ACF and PACF, can we author the AR fit they
lead to, reproduce statsmodels exactly, and confirm the model is a valid (stationary) generative
description of the alpha dynamics?** The goal is to introduce `arYuleWalker`, certify it bit-for-bit,
and read the AR structure.

## Challenge & approach

The AR(p) Yule-Walker fit solves the Yule-Walker equations formed from the biased demeaned
autocovariance (here via the Durbin-Levinson recursion on `autocorrelation`), giving the AR
coefficients and the innovation variance. We compute the AR(4) fit and check it against
`statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method="mle")` on the identical signal.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → ACF → Durbin-Levinson (Yule-Walker) → AR(4) coeffs + innovation variance
                    vs statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method="mle") → bit-exact (~5e-15 coeffs)
                    fit stationary (roots outside unit circle);  AR spectrum peaks ~12 Hz (alpha)
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[autocorrelation](../autocorrelation-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and [PACF](../pacf-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases
use. Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

The newly-authored op equals statsmodels for coefficients and variance, and the fit is a valid
stationary model. Values trace to [`artifacts/ar_summary.csv`](artifacts/ar_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`arYuleWalker` completes the ACF → PACF → AR-fit lane — the classical time-series toolchain — and it is
exact: bit-for-bit against statsmodels for both coefficients and variance. The transferable takeaway:
**the AR model is the ACF made generative. Choose its order from the PACF, fit it by Yule-Walker, check
it is stationary, and read its spectrum for a low-variance, sharp-peaked alternative to the
periodogram.**

## Open questions

- The AR fit yields a parametric spectrum with sharp peaks at fewer parameters than Welch; exposing it
  as an op (`arSpectrum`) and comparing its alpha peak against the folded Welch estimate, with AIC/BIC
  order selection over `arYuleWalker` fits, is the companion step. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| AR(p) Yule-Walker fit | `arYuleWalker()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| AR order (PACF cut-off) | `partialAutocorrelation()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Autocorrelation | `autocorrelation()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **order** — the AR order p (default 4); pick it from the `partialAutocorrelation` cut-off (the last
  lag whose PACF leaves the ±2/√N band), or by AIC/BIC over a range of orders.
- **method** — Yule-Walker with the biased (MLE) autocovariance, matching
  `statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method = "mle")`; the unbiased ("adjusted") variant differs.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

fit <- arYuleWalker(x, order = 4)
fit$ar          # AR coefficients (phi_1 .. phi_p)
fit$var_pred    # innovation variance
all(Mod(polyroot(c(1, -fit$ar))) > 1)   # stationary?
# reproduces statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method = "mle") bit-for-bit.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/ar_summary.csv`](artifacts/ar_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the first
two AR coefficients, the innovation variance, the bit-exact statsmodels(mle) match for both, the
stationarity, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op building on autocorrelation; MLE/biased
convention; machine-precision).
